notes:
Summary: Glassport is running a Dedicated capacity POC to validate throughput guarantees and rock-solid latency SLOs for a flight-control assistant and simulation augmentation workloads. They require VPC/private deployment with strict KMS and residency controls for avionics telemetry. Key asks: 99.9% p50/p95 latency targets for short prompt chains, deterministic autoscale for peak sim runs, reserved GPU planning for 150 concurrent inference streams.

POC scope: focused on throughput (tokens/sec) and latency under representative prompts + soak testing. We delivered a dedicated pool (8xA10g equiv) in staging with routing policies to fall back to smaller quantized model for overload. Test kit included health-checks, token accounting, and tracing hooks to Redwood Console.

Representative prompts: short control loop queries (~50 tokens), multi-turn sim scenario (~800 tokens), telemetry summarization batches (100x short records). Ops wants <80ms p50 on short control loop, <250ms p95; sim workload accepts higher latency but needs sustained throughput.

poc_details:
Dedicated pool: 8xA10g-equivalent GPUs reserved. Goal: support 150 concurrent streams for control loop + burst to 300 for simulation runs. Measured baseline: sustained 1200 tokens/sec with p50 65ms (short prompts), p95 220-260ms. Failure mode: after ~30h sustained throughput, thermal throttling-like drop in token/sec observed on one worker; suspected kernel selector/allocator edge-case. Next run will test revised kernel selection and aggressive KV cache hot-key eviction.
Metrics tracked: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, mem fragmentation, KV cache hit rate, request retries.
Acceptance criteria: p50 < 80ms and p95 < 250ms for short control prompts across 48h soak; no more than 1% request errors; autoscale fallback to quantized variant with <500ms tail latency when primary pool saturated.
poe_notes: SLA negotiation points: target latency SLOs (p50/p95) with credits for breaches, reserved GPU commit levels and overage pricing, maintenance windows / notify windows (72h), support response times (P1 1h), change control for kernel updates, audit log retention 3 years. Glassport wants explicit wording about deterministic routing and fallback behavior during peak. Procurement: needs legal review of SLA by 2026-04-15.
technical_requirements: VPC peering, mutual TLS, KMS key import, SSO via SAML, FIPS endpoints optional. Environment: air-gapped staging for final soak. Need per-route tracing hooks and token-level cost breakdowns exposed to Glassport console user. Quantization profiles acceptable for fallback only.
representative_prompts: simulation_scenario: multi-turn mission replanning with 6-step context (~800 tokens)
telemetry_batch: 100 short sensor records -> summarize anomalies (~1000 tokens aggregated)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: sustained thermal/GPU throttling under prolonged high-throughput runs leads to p95 spikes. Mitigation: staggered worker drain, stricter KV cache eviction, fallbacks to quantized model, reserve + burst capacity plan. Risk: procurement/legal timeline slips. Mitigation: provide draft SLA and standard enterprise contract early.
final_notes: Customer receptive to dedicated commit if soak passes and SLA language covers deterministic fallbacks. AE to push for exec review and procurement alignment. Keep infra loop tight — infra patch scheduled 2026-03-14, retest 2026-03-17.
